1	import XCTest
2	
3	/// UI test for the activity bar's **Changes dirty dot**. The fixture (`-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`)
4	/// auto-selects the jj fixture workroom, whose seeded `WorkroomStatus` is `dirty: true`
5	/// (`UITestFixture.workroomStatus`), so on launch the Changes icon must signal the uncommitted
6	/// working tree. The dot itself is decorative (a11y-hidden); the state is announced on the icon
7	/// button's accessibility **value** ("has changes"), which is what this test reads.
8	///
9	/// Also guards that the dot is scoped to Changes only — no peer icon inherits the dirty value even
10	/// though the selected workroom is dirty.
11	///
12	/// The peer icons are **discovered from the accessibility tree**, not named. This test used to probe
13	/// `activitySection.history` by name, which stopped existing when History moved out of the activity bar
14	/// and into the Changes stack (`0fc3b97a`): reading `.value` on a element that isn't there throws
15	/// "Failed to get matching snapshot", so the test failed for 16 days while saying nothing about the dot.
16	/// Enumerating whatever sections the bar renders keeps the assertion honest through the next such move.
17	///
18	/// Run with `make app-uitest` on a real GUI login session — XCUITest can't drive a headless run, so
19	/// this is excluded from `make app-test` (the unit gate) via a separate scheme.
20	final class ActivityBarDirtyDotUITests: XCTestCase {
21	  override func setUpWithError() throws { continueAfterFailure = false }
22	
23	  private func launchedApp() -> XCUIApplication {
24	    let app = XCUIApplication()
25	    app.launchArguments += ["-WorkroomUITestFixture", "1"]
26	    app.launchArguments += ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES"]
27	    app.launch()
28	    app.activate()
29	    return app
30	  }
31	
32	  /// A bar icon by its accessibility id (`activitySection.<rawValue>`).
33	  private func icon(_ app: XCUIApplication, _ raw: String) -> XCUIElement {
34	    app.descendants(matching: .any).matching(identifier: "activitySection.\(raw)").firstMatch
35	  }
36	
37	  /// Every activity-bar icon currently in the tree, by identifier — whatever sections the bar renders.
38	  private func barIcons(_ app: XCUIApplication) -> [(id: String, value: String)] {
39	    app.descendants(matching: .any)
40	      .matching(NSPredicate(format: "identifier BEGINSWITH %@", "activitySection."))
41	      .allElementsBoundByIndex
42	      .map { (id: $0.identifier, value: $0.value as? String ?? "") }
43	  }
44	
45	  /// Wait until `el`'s accessibility value contains `text`. The dirty state rides the icon button's
46	  /// value ("has changes"), so this asserts the dot's wiring directly.
47	  @discardableResult
48	  private func waitValue(_ el: XCUIElement, contains text: String, _ timeout: TimeInterval = 6)
49	    -> Bool
50	  {
51	    let p = NSPredicate(format: "value CONTAINS %@", text)
52	    return XCTWaiter().wait(
53	      for: [XCTNSPredicateExpectation(predicate: p, object: el)], timeout: timeout) == .completed
54	  }
55	
56	  /// The dirty fixture workroom is selected on launch, so the Changes icon reports "has changes" and
57	  /// the other sections don't — the dot is Changes-scoped, driven by the selected target's status.
58	  func testChangesIconShowsDirtyForDirtyWorkroom() throws {
59	    let app = launchedApp()
60	    XCTAssertTrue(app.wait(for: .runningForeground, timeout: 10))
61	
62	    let changes = icon(app, "changes")
63	    XCTAssertTrue(changes.waitForExistence(timeout: 10), "activity bar should render")
64	
65	    // The seeded workroom is dirty → the Changes icon announces it on its accessibility value.
66	    XCTAssertTrue(
67	      waitValue(changes, contains: "has changes"),
68	      "Changes icon should report the dirty working tree")
69	
70	    // The dot is scoped to Changes: no peer section inherits the dirty value. Peers are read off the
71	    // tree rather than named, so a section leaving the bar can't turn this into a query for an element
72	    // that doesn't exist (which is how it broke before — see the type doc).
73	    let peers = barIcons(app).filter { $0.id != "activitySection.changes" }
74	    XCTAssertFalse(
75	      peers.isEmpty,
76	      "the bar must render at least one peer section, or this assertion proves nothing")
77	    for peer in peers {
78	      XCTAssertFalse(
79	        peer.value.contains("has changes"),
80	        "\(peer.id) must not carry the dirty dot — it is scoped to Changes")
81	    }
82	  }
83	}

Per the review instructions, test files are explicitly excluded from security review ("Do NOT report: ... test/mock files"). The change enumerates accessibility tree elements to make the assertion resilient to UI restructuring — there are no sinks, entry points, or attacker-influenceable data flows here.
